test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 26 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: What does the term 'formula unit mass' refer to?

options.text: Mass of a single proton in an atom
Sum of atomic masses of all atoms in the compound
Mass of one molecule of a covalent compound
Total mass of atoms in one mole of a compound

solution:
The correct answer is __**Sum of atomic masses of all atoms in the compound**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **formula unit mass** of a substance is defined as the **sum of the atomic masses** of all atoms in a formula unit of a compound.
 
• This term is specifically used for substances that are **ionic** in nature, where discrete molecules do not exist. Instead, these substances exist as a **three-dimensional lattice** of ions.
 
• The calculation method for formula unit mass is identical to that of **molecular mass**; the only difference lies in the terminology used for **ionic compounds** versus **covalent compounds**.
 
• It is expressed in **atomic mass units (u)**, where **1 u** is defined as exactly **1/12th** the mass of one atom of **carbon-12**.
 
• For example, in **Sodium Chloride (NaCl)**, the formula unit consists of one **Sodium (Na)** ion and one **Chloride (Cl)** ion. The formula unit mass is calculated by adding the atomic mass of **Na (23 u)** and **Cl (35.5 u)**, resulting in **58.5 u**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Molecular Mass:**
 
 
• This refers to the sum of atomic masses of all atoms in a **molecule** of a substance. It is used for **covalent compounds** like **Water (H2O)** or **Methane (CH4)**.
 
• For **H2O**, the molecular mass is **(2 x 1.008 u) + 16.00 u = 18.016 u**.
 
 
 
• **Atomic Mass:**
 
 
• It is the mass of a **single atom** of a chemical element. It is approximately equivalent to the number of **protons and neutrons** in the nucleus.
 
• The **unified atomic mass unit (u)** is the standard unit used to indicate mass on an atomic or molecular scale.
 
 
 
• **Molar Mass:**
 
 
• This is the mass of **one mole** of a substance (element or compound). It is numerically equal to the atomic or molecular mass but is expressed in **grams per mole (g/mol)**.
 
• One mole contains exactly **6.02214076 x 10^23** elementary entities, a value known as **Avogadro's number**.
 
 
 
• **Ionic Compounds and Lattice Structures:**
 
 
• In compounds like **Calcium Chloride (CaCl2)**, the formula unit mass is calculated as the sum of the atomic mass of **Calcium (40 u)** and twice the atomic mass of **Chlorine (2 x 35.5 u)**, totaling **111 u**.
 
• These compounds do not form individual molecules but rather repeating units in a **crystalline structure**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Relative Atomic Mass:** The atomic masses used in these calculations are **relative** values compared to the **Carbon-12** isotope.
 
• **Stoichiometry:** Understanding formula unit mass is crucial for **stoichiometric calculations** in chemistry, allowing scientists to determine the **mass-to-mole** ratios in chemical reactions.
 
• **Precision:** While whole numbers are often used for simplicity (e.g., **O = 16**), high-precision chemistry uses decimal values (e.g., **O = 15.999**) to account for **isotopic abundance**.
